=== [0:12] 참지 못하고 오늘 와버렸다 ===
meaning: I couldn't hold back and ended up coming on today.
tone: Casual, playful opening; speaker talks to herself/fans in 반말 (informal speech).
--- word ---
term: 참지 못하고
type: verb + negative ability + connective
breakdown: 참다 (to endure) + -지 못하다 (cannot) + -고
meaning: couldn't hold back and...
notes: -지 못하다 is the longer, slightly more formal way to say 'cannot'. The short form 못 + verb is more casual. -고 links actions in sequence.
--- word ---
term: 오늘
type: noun/adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: today
notes: Works as a time word without any particle. Neutral register.
--- word ---
term: 와버렸다
type: verb
breakdown: 오다 (to come) + -아/어 버리다 (end up doing) + -었- (past) + -다 (plain declarative)
meaning: ended up coming
notes: -아/어 버리다 shows completion, often with regret, relief or 'I just did it'. Here it means she gave in. -다 plain form is used in diary-like or self-talking style; it is not polite speech. Casual alternative: 와 버렸어.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -아/어 버리다
meaning: do something completely or 'end up' doing it, often with a feeling of regret or release
example: 먹어 버렸어. (I ended up eating it.)
level: Intermediate
--- grammar ---
pattern: -지 못하다
meaning: cannot do; unable to
example: 가지 못했어요. (I couldn't go.)
level: Beginner

=== [0:20] 못 참고 와버렸어 ===
meaning: I couldn't hold back and ended up coming.
tone: Casual, 반말; a repeat with a slightly more spoken feel.
--- word ---
term: 못
type: adverb (negation)
breakdown: 
meaning: can't, unable to
notes: Placed before a verb for inability. It is the colloquial counterpart of -지 못하다. Don't confuse with 안 (simply not doing something by choice).
--- word ---
term: 참고
type: verb + connective
breakdown: 참다 (to endure) + -고
meaning: hold back and...
notes: -고 connects the action to the next one. 참다 means to endure or restrain oneself.
--- word ---
term: 와버렸어
type: verb
breakdown: 오다 + -아 버리다 + -었- + -어
meaning: ended up coming
notes: -어 is the casual 반말 ending, in contrast to the plain -다. Adding -요 would make it polite: 와 버렸어요. Often contracted in speech to 와버렸어.
--- grammar ---
pattern: 못 + verb
meaning: short form of negation for inability
example: 못 먹어. (I can't eat.)
level: Beginner

=== [0:23] 어떡하지? ===
meaning: What should I do?
tone: Casual, mock-worried, rhetorical, teasing herself.
--- word ---
term: 어떡하지?
type: verb phrase + sentence ending
breakdown: 어떻게 하다 (to do how) contracted to 어떡하다 + -지
meaning: What should I do?
notes: 어떡해 is the contraction of 어떻게 해 (how do I do it). Learners often confuse 어떡해 (what do I do) with 어떻게 (how). -지 here is a soft ending asking oneself or inviting agreement. Used playfully when something is a bit embarrassing or unavoidable.

=== [0:40] 오늘 올 거라고 생각했다고? 거짓말 치지 마 ===
meaning: You're saying you thought I'd come on today? Don't lie.
tone: Casual, teasing; echoes a viewer's comment and playfully pushes back.
--- word ---
term: 오늘
type: noun/adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: today
notes: Time word; needs no particle.
--- word ---
term: 올
type: verb (modifier)
breakdown: 오다 + -ㄹ (future/presumptive modifier)
meaning: that (I) would come
notes: -(으)ㄹ turns a verb into a modifier for future or expected actions.
--- word ---
term: 거라고
type: bound noun + copula + quotation particle
breakdown: 것 + 이다 + -라고
meaning: that it would be
notes: -ㄹ 거라고 is a quoted 'will/would'. 거 is the contraction of 것 (thing). Here it reports what the viewer thought.
--- word ---
term: 생각했다고?
type: verb + quotative ending
breakdown: 생각하다 (to think) + -았- + -다고
meaning: you thought that...?
notes: -다고? with rising tone echoes what someone said and asks for confirmation, often with disbelief or teasing. Per the bible, this is her echoing a chat comment.
--- word ---
term: 거짓말
type: noun
breakdown: 
meaning: lie
notes: Literally 'false words'. 거짓말하다 means to lie.
--- word ---
term: 치지
type: verb
breakdown: 치다 + -지
meaning: tell (a lie)
notes: 거짓말(을) 치다 is a casual collocation for 'to tell a lie', more colloquial than 거짓말하다. The particle 을 is dropped in speech.
--- word ---
term: 마
type: verb ending (negative imperative)
breakdown: 말다 + -아 (casual)
meaning: don't
notes: -지 마 is the casual 'don't do'. Polite is -지 마세요. It can sound blunt, but here it is playful.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -다고?
meaning: echo question: 'you're saying that...?'
example: 안 간다고? (You're saying you're not going?)
level: Intermediate
--- grammar ---
pattern: -지 마
meaning: casual prohibition: don't do it
example: 울지 마. (Don't cry.)
level: Beginner

=== [0:48] 아니 술은? 몇 잔? ===
meaning: No, what about the alcohol? How many glasses?
tone: Casual, reading a chat question aloud and echoing it.
--- word ---
term: 아니
type: interjection
breakdown: 
meaning: no / hold on
notes: Used at the start of a reply, even when not literally saying no. It can mean 'well' or 'wait', and is common in casual speech.
--- word ---
term: 술은?
type: noun + topic particle
breakdown: 술 (alcohol) + -은 (topic)
meaning: as for alcohol?
notes: The topic particle 은/는 plus a rising tone repeats the viewer's question: 'what about the drinks?'. 술 refers to alcoholic drinks in general.
--- word ---
term: 몇
type: determiner
breakdown: 
meaning: how many
notes: Must be followed by a counter or noun. Not used alone.
--- word ---
term: 잔?
type: counter noun
breakdown: 
meaning: glasses
notes: 잔 is the counter for glasses or cups of drinks. 몇 잔 means 'how many glasses'. Drinking is often counted in 잔 or 병 (bottles).
--- grammar ---
pattern: noun + 은/는?
meaning: 'what about X?' follow-up question
example: 밥은? (What about the meal?)
level: Beginner

=== [0:51] 밥 먹고 왔어 ===
meaning: I ate a meal and came.
tone: Casual, matter-of-fact answer; refers to the team dinner earlier.
--- word ---
term: 밥
type: noun
breakdown: 
meaning: meal / cooked rice
notes: Literally cooked rice but commonly means 'a meal'. 밥 먹었어? is a common casual greeting-like question.
--- word ---
term: 먹고
type: verb + connective
breakdown: 먹다 + -고
meaning: ate and then...
notes: -고 links two actions in order: eat, then come. Particle 을 is omitted after 밥 in speech.
--- word ---
term: 왔어
type: verb
breakdown: 오다 + -았- + -어
meaning: came
notes: 오 + 았 contracts to 왔. -어 is the casual 반말 ending; polite would be 왔어요. Notice 먹고 왔어 means 'ate and came', not 'came to eat'.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V-고 오다
meaning: do something and then come
example: 밥 먹고 왔어요. (I ate and came.)
level: Beginner

=== [0:54] 오리 먹었어 오리를 한 두 마리는 먹은 것 같아 ===
meaning: I ate duck. I think I ate about one or two ducks.
tone: Casual, humorous exaggeration; hedged with a vague estimate.
--- word ---
term: 오리
type: noun
breakdown: 
meaning: duck
notes: Here it refers to duck meat from the restaurant dinner. 오리고기 is duck meat; people often just say 오리.
--- word ---
term: 먹었어
type: verb
breakdown: 먹다 + -었- + -어
meaning: ate
notes: Casual 반말 past. Polite: 먹었어요.
--- word ---
term: 오리를
type: noun + object particle
breakdown: 오리 + -를
meaning: duck (object)
notes: Restating the object with 를 after the verb is a spoken afterthought, where she adds detail. Casual speech often rearranges order like this.
--- word ---
term: 한 두
type: determiner phrase
breakdown: 한 (one) + 두 (two)
meaning: one or two
notes: Native Korean numbers shortened before counters. 한두 (written together) means 'one or two' or 'a couple'.
--- word ---
term: 마리는
type: counter + topic particle
breakdown: 마리 + -는
meaning: (at least) ... animals
notes: 마리 is the counter for animals, including ducks served as food. The particle 는 adds a nuance of 'at least' or 'as for the amount'.
--- word ---
term: 먹은
type: verb (modifier)
breakdown: 먹다 + -은 (past modifier)
meaning: that I ate
notes: -은 makes a past modifier for the following noun 것.
--- word ---
term: 것 같아
type: bound noun + adjective
breakdown: 것 (thing) + 같다 (to seem) + -아
meaning: I think / it seems
notes: -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 softens a statement or guesses about the past. Very common hedging in spoken Korean. Polite: 것 같아요.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -(으)ㄴ 것 같다
meaning: it seems that (someone) did; I think
example: 비가 온 것 같아요. (It seems it rained.)
level: Intermediate

=== [2:07] 나 지금 손 씻고 있어. ===
meaning: I'm washing my hands right now.
tone: Casual, explaining what she is doing on stream.
--- word ---
term: 나
type: pronoun
breakdown: 
meaning: I
notes: Casual form of 'I', used with friends or fans in 반말. The polite/humble form is 저. Subjects like this are often dropped in conversation, but she states it for emphasis.
--- word ---
term: 지금
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: now, right now
notes: Means the present moment. Compare 이제, which means 'now' as a change of state ('from now on', 'by now'). 지금 is simply 'at this moment'.
--- word ---
term: 손
type: noun
breakdown: 
meaning: hand

--- word ---
term: 씻고
type: verb + connective
breakdown: 씻다 (to wash) + 고
meaning: washing (and...)
notes: Here 씻고 combines with 있어 to make the progressive. 씻다 is used for washing the body, hands, or face. For washing dishes or clothes, use 설거지하다 or 빨다.
--- word ---
term: 있어
type: auxiliary verb ending
breakdown: 있다 (to be/exist) + 어
meaning: am (doing)
notes: Casual 반말 ending. Polite version: 있어요. With -고, it forms the progressive 'is doing'.
--- grammar ---

=== [2:50] 본격 칫솔 라이브 ===
meaning: A full-on toothbrushing live
tone: Playful, noun phrase with no verb, like a title or caption.
--- word ---
term: 본격
type: noun (Sino-Korean)
breakdown: 本格
meaning: full-fledged, in earnest
notes: Often used as a joking caption on variety shows, like 본격 먹방 (full-on eating show). Playfully exaggerates a trivial activity to sound like a main event.

=== [3:02] 마시는게 아니라 너무 많이 먹어서 ===

--- grammar ---

--- word ---
term: 다시
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: again
notes: Casual and neutral. It means doing something over or returning to a state. Related: 또 (again, another time, often for repeated occurrences) and 다시 한번 (once more). Learners often mix up 다시 (redo or return) with 또 (repeat of a similar event).

=== [5:17] 노란 조명으로 왔어. ===
meaning: I came back with the yellow lighting.
tone: Casual 반말, playful; refers to her running yellow-lighting gag.
--- word ---
term: 노란
type: adjective (modifier form)
breakdown: 노랗다 (to be yellow) + -ㄴ
meaning: yellow
notes: 노랗다 is an ㅎ-irregular adjective: the ㅎ drops before -ㄴ, giving 노란. Related: 노래 (song) is a different word; 노란색 means the color yellow. Casual and neutral.
--- word ---
term: 조명으로
type: noun + particle
breakdown: 조명 (lighting) + -으로
meaning: with/by the lighting
notes: -으로 marks means or manner here. It is also used for direction (to) and for tools. 조명 means lighting in the sense of lamps or stage lights. Because the lights are part of her home, it implies she's back in her usual yellow-lit room.
--- word ---
term: 왔어
type: verb + casual ending
breakdown: 오다 (to come) + -았어
meaning: came
notes: Past tense, informal polite-casual 반말. Full polite form: 왔어요 (I came). Formal: 왔습니다. 오다 is used from the listener's viewpoint, which suits a streamer greeting her audience: I've come to you.
--- grammar ---
pattern: N(으)로 오다
meaning: to come with/in/by N

=== [5:18] 너무나도 익숙하지? ===
meaning: It feels so familiar, right?
tone: Casual 반말, teasing tag question to the chat.
--- word ---
term: 너무나도
type: adverb
breakdown: 너무 (too, very) + 나 + 도
meaning: so very much
notes: An emphatic form of 너무. 너무나 is stronger than 너무, and adding -도 intensifies it further. Casual and spoken. Though 너무 literally means too much, native speakers use it everywhere to mean very.
--- word ---
term: 익숙하지
type: adjective + ending
breakdown: 익숙하다 (to be familiar) + -지

--- grammar ---
pattern: -지?
meaning: tag question seeking agreement: right? / isn't it?
example: 맛있지? (It's delicious, right?)

term: 너무나도
type: adverb
breakdown: 너무 + 나 + 도

=== [5:36] 우리 스텝들은 두 팩을 먹었대. ===
meaning: They say our staff ate two packs.
tone: Casual 반말, reporting secondhand information with amusement.
--- word ---
term: 우리
type: pronoun
breakdown: 
meaning: our
notes: Literally we or our. Koreans use 우리 for groups they belong to, such as 우리 가족 (my family) and 우리 회사 (my company), even where English says my. Here it marks the staff as her team.
--- word ---
term: 스텝들은
type: noun + plural + particle
breakdown: 스텝 (staff) + -들 (plural) + -은 (topic)
meaning: the staff (as for)
notes: 스텝 is a loanword from English staff, often spelled 스태프 in standard Korean. -들 pluralizes people, and -은 marks the topic, setting up what is said about them. Korean often has no plural marker, but -들 is used here for the group of people.
--- word ---
term: 두
type: counter modifier
breakdown: 둘 (two) → 두
meaning: two
notes: Native Korean number 둘 shortens to 두 before a counter or noun. Used with counters like 팩, 개, 명. Learners should not use sino-Korean 이 with this counter.
--- word ---
term: 팩을
type: counter noun + particle
breakdown: 팩 (pack) + -을 (object)
meaning: packs
notes: 팩 is a loanword from English pack. It works as a counter for packaged items. Order is number + counter + object particle: 두 팩을.
--- word ---
term: 먹었대
type: verb + quotative contraction
breakdown: 먹다 (to eat) + -었다고 하다 → -었대
meaning: they say (someone) ate
notes: -었대 is the contracted form of -었다고 해, reporting hearsay in casual speech. Full form: 먹었다고 해. It tells the listener she heard this from someone else. Polite: 먹었대요. Not to be confused with -냬 (asks) or -래 (commands).
--- grammar ---
pattern: -다고 해 → -대
meaning: casual reported speech: they say that…
example: 비가 온대. (They say it will rain.)
level: Intermediate

=== [5:45] 너무 맛있어서. ===

=== [5:57] 그 혈당 스파이크 이런 거를 이렇게 막아주는 ... 그런 ===

--- word ---
term: 그
type: determiner (filler)
breakdown: 
meaning: that / um
notes: 그 is used as a filler word, like 'um' or 'that thing', while thinking. Very common in spoken Korean.
--- word ---
term: 혈당
type: noun
breakdown: 혈 (blood) + 당 (sugar)
meaning: blood sugar
notes: Sino-Korean word (derived from Chinese characters). Often used in diet and health talk.

meaning: spike

term: 이런
type: determiner
breakdown: 이렇다 (to be like this) → 이런
meaning: this kind of
notes: Modifies the noun that follows. Related: 그런 (that kind of), 저런 (that kind of, over there).

meaning: Present-tense modifier: a noun that does the verb

meaning: siru-tteok, steamed layered rice cake
notes: Steamed rice cake made in a steamer pot, often layered with beans or red bean. It tends to be dry and crumbly, which fits her dry-mouth complaint.
--- word ---
term: 느낌
type: noun
breakdown: 느끼다 (to feel) → 느낌
meaning: feeling, vibe, texture
notes: Very common: N + 느낌 means 'a N-like feel'. Often used for taste, texture or atmosphere. Example: 가을 느낌 (autumn vibe).
--- grammar ---
pattern: N 느낌
meaning: a feeling or vibe of N
example: 봄 느낌이에요. (It has a spring feel.)
level: Beginner

=== [6:44] 그래서 ===
meaning: So…
tone: Fragment; trailing connector leading into the next thought.
--- word ---
term: 그래서
type: conjunction
breakdown: 그래 + -서
meaning: so, therefore
notes: Links a reason to a result. Often used in speech as a pause-filler when the speaker is gathering their next thought. Works in all registers.

=== [6:45] 얘기할 시간도 없는데 ===
meaning: We don't even have time to talk, but…
tone: Casual; incomplete, continues into the next clause with a contrast.
--- word ---
term: 얘기할
type: verb (modifier form)
breakdown: 얘기하다 (to talk) → 얘기하 + -ㄹ
meaning: to talk (modifying 'time')
notes: 얘기 is the contraction of 이야기 (story, talk). The future/potential modifier -ㄹ describes 'time to talk'. Casual and common in speech.
--- word ---
term: 시간도
type: noun + particle
breakdown: 시간 (time) + 도 (also, even)
meaning: even time
notes: 도 means 'also' or 'even'. With a negative, it means 'not even'. 시간이 없다 means 'there is no time'.
--- word ---
term: 없는데
type: adjective + connective ending
breakdown: 없다 (to not exist) → 없 + -는데
meaning: there isn't, but…
notes: -는데 sets up background or contrast and often leaves the sentence open. Here it implies 'but still…' and continues in the next line.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -는데
meaning: background or contrast connective; 'and/but'
example: 비가 오는데 나가요? (It's raining, but are you going out?)

--- grammar ---
pattern: V-ㄹ 시간
meaning: time to do something
example: 먹을 시간이 없어요. (There's no time to eat.)
level: Beginner

--- word ---
term: 근데
type: conjunction
breakdown: 그런데 → 근데
meaning: but, by the way

--- word ---
term: 그
type: determiner
breakdown: 
meaning: that
notes: Points to something already known to both speaker and listener. Here it refers to the tteok they know about.
--- word ---
term: 떡
type: noun
breakdown: 
meaning: tteok, rice cake
notes: Repeated as she restarts the phrase, a normal self-correction in speech. Rice cakes vary widely: 인절미, 백설기, 시루떡.
--- word ---
term: 씹느라
type: verb + connective ending
breakdown: 씹다 (to chew) → 씹 + -느라

meaning: eating up, consuming
notes: Literally 'to catch and eat'. Figuratively, 시간을 잡아먹다 means to eat up or waste time. Informal, colorful expression.
--- word ---
term: 것 같아서

breakdown: 것 같다 (seems like) → 것 같 + -아서
meaning: because it seems like…

--- grammar ---
pattern: V-느라
meaning: because of being busy doing V (usually with a negative result)
example: 게임하느라 못 잤어요. (I couldn't sleep because I was busy playing games.)
level: Intermediate
--- grammar ---
pattern: V-는 것 같다
meaning: it seems that; I feel like

--- grammar ---

breakdown: 뭔가 + 의
meaning: of some kind of something
notes: 뭔가 is short for 무언가 (something), and is also used to mean 'somehow, kind of'. The possessive 의 links it to the next noun. Casual, vague filler.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -(이)라는 + noun
meaning: a noun called/saying X
example: 행복이라는 단어 (the word 'happiness')

=== [29:53] 좀 진지했어. 되게 진지했어. ===

meaning: was serious

=== [30:06] 이제 또 막상 나눠주니까 또 너무 행복하대 ===

--- word ---
term: 이제
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: now, at that point
notes: Here it works as a story-marker like 'then' or 'by this point'. 이제 emphasizes a change of state. Compare 지금, which means literally 'right now'.
--- word ---
term: 또
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: again, also (filler)
notes: Literally 'again', but repeated here as a conversational filler that adds a sense of 'and then, once again'. It adds rhythm rather than strict meaning.
--- word ---
term: 막상
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: when it actually comes to it
notes: 막상 describes the reality that appears once you actually do something, often differing from expectation. Example: 막상 가 보니 좋았어 (once I actually went, it was nice).
--- word ---
term: 나눠주니까
type: verb + connective
breakdown: 나누어 주다 → 나눠주다 + -(으)니까
meaning: because/when I shared (them)
notes: 나눠주다 means to share out or give to others (나누다 is to divide/share, 주다 is to give). 나눠 is a contraction of 나누어. -(으)니까 here means 'when/after I did X, I found that…', a discovery sense.
--- word ---
term: 너무
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: so, very
notes: Originally 'too much', but in modern speech it is a common positive intensifier like 'so'. Natural with positive feelings.
--- word ---
term: 행복하대

breakdown: 행복하다 + -대 (-다고 해 → -대)
meaning: (I'm) happy, they say / apparently happy
notes: -대 is the contraction of -다고 해, used to report what someone said. Here it likely echoes a thought or comment, adding a self-mocking tone, as if reporting herself. Casual 반말 only.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -(으)니까
meaning: because; or when/after doing X, found that Y
example: 먹어 보니까 맛있었어. (When I tried it, it was tasty.)
level: Beginner
--- grammar ---
pattern: -대 (-다고 해)
meaning: reported speech: they say that…
example: 비가 온대. (They say it's going to rain.)
level: Intermediate

example: 비가 오니까 우산을 가져가. (Since it's raining, take an umbrella.)

=== [35:45] 칼로리가 몇이죠? ===
meaning: So how many calories is that?
tone: Polite-casual, rhetorical, quizzing the audience in a showy way.
--- word ---
term: 칼로리가
type: noun + subject particle
breakdown: 칼로리 + 가
meaning: the calories (subject)
notes: 칼로리 is a loanword for calories. 가 marks the subject, which is the focus of the question.
--- word ---
term: 몇이죠

breakdown: 몇 + 이다 + -죠 (-지요)
meaning: how many is it?

--- grammar ---
pattern: -죠 / -지요
meaning: soft polite ending; asks for confirmation or poses a rhetorical question

=== [35:58] 먹어볼게요. ===
meaning: I'll try eating it.

term: 아니었거든
type: verb ending
breakdown: 아니다 + 었 + 거든
meaning: because I wasn't (you see)
notes: -거든 gives a reason or background in casual speech, as if saying 'you see, it's because...'. Used in 반말 or 거든요 (polite).
--- grammar ---
pattern: -거든(요)
meaning: explains a reason or background that the listener may not know
example: 저 바빠요. 시험이 있거든요 (I'm busy. I have an exam, you see)
level: Intermediate

term: 이럴

meaning: being like this

--- word ---
term: 거면

meaning: if (it's going to be)

=== [1:08:03] 무대를 보는 건지 모르겠는 ===

term: 무대를

meaning: the stage
notes: 무대 means stage. Commonly used for performances; 무대 위 means 'on stage'.
--- word ---
term: 보는
type: verb + modifier ending

meaning: looking at
notes: Pairs with the previous line's 보는 건지 to form 'A인지 B인지'.
--- word ---
term: 건지
type: bound noun + ending
breakdown: 것 + 인지
meaning: whether it is that…
notes: Contraction of 것인지. Repeating it makes an 'is it A or is it B' construction.

=== [1:08:42] 그 표정들이랑 이런 게 너무 생각나는 거지. ===

--- word ---
term: 그

breakdown:

notes: Refers to the fan chants that fans shout along to a song. 응원 means cheering and 법 means method or rule. This is a fandom-specific word.
--- word ---
term: 엄청
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: extremely
notes: Casual intensifier, similar to 'super' or 'really'. Common in speech but too casual for formal writing.
--- word ---
term: 커져
type: verb
breakdown: 크다 + -어지다 → 커지다 → 커져 (casual)
meaning: gets bigger / louder
notes: -어지다 means 'to become'. 커지다 is 'grow bigger' and for sound means 'get louder'. Ending -어 is casual 반말.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -어지다
meaning: Becomes / gets (change of state).
example: 날씨가 추워졌어요. (The weather got cold.)

=== [1:10:02] 그래서 이거야말로 프로가 아닐까 싶어 ===

--- word ---
term: 그래서
type: conjunction
breakdown: 그러하다 + -아서
meaning: so / therefore
notes: Connects a conclusion to the previous statement. Very common in speech.
--- word ---
term: 이거야말로

breakdown: 이거 + -야말로

meaning: I wonder if / I'm thinking maybe; a tentative opinion.

--- grammar ---

=== [1:10:07] 내가 정말 배워야 배워야 하는 거 같아 ===

=== [1:12:05] 내가 무대를 저렇게 했었나? ===

notes: 되다 means to become or be okay. '-(으)면 안 돼요?' is a common way to ask permission or suggest an alternative, like 'Is it not okay if…?'. Polite 해요 style.
--- grammar ---

=== [1:21:28] 근데 아빠가 그러시더라고 ===

breakdown: 그런데 (contracted)

=== [1:33:56] 토순이라는거는 자체는 너무 귀여운데 ===
meaning: The Tosuni thing itself is really cute, but…
tone: Casual, contrasting. The line continues into a 'but' clause.
--- word ---
term: 토순이라는거는
type: noun + quotative modifier + topic
breakdown: 토순이 + 이라는 (이라고 하는) + 거 (것) + 는
meaning: the thing called Tosuni
notes: -(이)라는 means 'called / named', a contraction of -(이)라고 하는. 거 is the spoken form of 것 (thing). 는 is the topic particle. Learners often write 거는 as one word, but it is 거 plus 는.
--- word ---
term: 자체는
type: noun + topic particle
breakdown: 자체 (itself) + 는
meaning: in itself
notes: 자체 follows a noun to mean 'itself, per se'. Topic particle 는 sets up the contrast with the coming 'but' part.
--- word ---
term: 너무
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: really, so
notes: Textbooks say it means 'too much' (negative), but in speech it is a common intensifier for positive things too, like 'so cute'.
--- word ---
term: 귀여운데
type: adjective + connective ending
breakdown: 귀엽다 (cute) → 귀여우 + ㄴ데
meaning: is cute, but…
notes: ㅂ-irregular: 귀엽다 becomes 귀여운. -(으)ㄴ데 sets the background or contrast, and here signals 'but' with more to come.
--- grammar ---
pattern: -(으)ㄴ/는데
meaning: Connective that sets up contrast or background, 'but / and'
example: 예쁜데 비싸요. (It's pretty, but expensive.)
level: Beginner

tone: Informal, trailing. It is a fragment that continues into the next line.
--- word ---
term: 이렇게
type: adverb
breakdown: 이렇다 (to be like this) + 게
meaning: like this, this way
notes: Casual and standard. It refers to something present or just mentioned. Related: 그렇게 (like that), 저렇게 (like that over there).
--- word ---
term: 쓰다가
type: verb + connective ending
breakdown: 쓰다 (to use) + -다가
meaning: while using, and then (switching)
notes: -다가 means an action is interrupted or followed by a change. Do not confuse 쓰다 (to use, to write) with 쓰다 (to be bitter); context decides. Casual speech often shortens it to -다. Related: 쓰다가 바꾸다 means to use it for a while and then change.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V-다가
meaning: does something, then stops or switches to another action
example: 자다가 깼어요. (I was sleeping and woke up.)
level: Intermediate

=== [1:37:48] 나중에는 또 뭐 ===
meaning: Later on, again, like...
tone: Informal, thinking aloud. 뭐 is a filler word and the sentence continues.
--- word ---
term: 나중에는
type: noun/adverb + particle
breakdown: 나중 (later) + 에 (at) + 는 (topic/contrast)
meaning: later on, eventually
notes: 나중에 means 'later' (in the future). 는 adds contrast, as in 'later on, though'. Compare 이따가 (later today, shortly) and 나중에 (a longer or vaguer later).
--- word ---
term: 또
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: again, also
notes: Means 'again' or 'additionally'. Used heavily in casual talk as a filler for emphasis. Do not confuse it with 도 (also, a particle).
--- word ---
term: 뭐
type: pronoun/filler
breakdown: 무엇 (what), contracted to 뭐
meaning: like, you know, whatever
notes: Literally 'what'. In casual speech it works as a filler while the speaker thinks, like English 'like' or 'whatever'. 뭐 is the contracted form of 무엇 (what). Casual only.

=== [1:37:50] 더 좋은 거 생기면 또 바꾸면 되잖아. 그치? ===

tone: Casual, reassuring, and seeking agreement from fans.
--- word ---
term: 더
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: more
notes: Comparative marker placed before adjectives: 더 좋다 (better).
--- word ---
term: 좋은
type: adjective (modifier form)
breakdown: 좋다 (to be good) + -은
meaning: good (modifying 거)
notes: -은 turns an adjective into a modifier before a noun. Here 더 좋은 거 means 'something better'.
--- word ---
term: 거
type: noun (bound)
breakdown: 것 (thing) contracted to 거
meaning: thing, one
notes: 거 is the spoken contraction of 것 (thing). Very common in casual speech. Full form 것 is used in writing.
--- word ---
term: 생기면
type: verb + conditional ending
breakdown: 생기다 (to come into being) + -면
meaning: if it comes up / if we get

breakdown: 바꾸다 (to change, to swap) + -면
meaning: if we change

--- grammar ---
pattern: V-(으)면 되다
meaning: it's fine if you just do V; all you need to do is V

--- grammar ---
pattern: -잖아
meaning: you know / as you know, reminding the listener
example: 어제 말했잖아. (I told you yesterday, remember?)
level: Intermediate
